name: FEMA National Risk Index (NRI) v1.20

geography_rules.state: Two-digit STATEFIPS joined exactly to TIGER/Line 2024 state GEOID. Territories outside CHIP's 2024 boundary layer are staged as source_only and not published.
geography_rules.county: Five-digit STCOFIPS joined exactly to TIGER/Line 2024 county-equivalent GEOID. Connecticut appears as planning regions (09110-09190). Unmatched rows are staged as source_only and not published.
geography_rules.tract: Eleven-digit TRACTFIPS joined exactly to TIGER/Line 2024 census tract GEOID. Connecticut appears as planning-region tracts. Unmatched rows are staged as source_only and not published.

boundary.vintage: TIGER/Line 2024 states, county equivalents, and census tracts (Connecticut planning regions)

limitations: These are FEMA's scores, percentiles, and dollar estimates for natural-hazard risk. They are not forecasts, and they say nothing about any one property.
A score is a national percentile among areas at the same level. A state percentile compares an area only with others in its state.
Expected annual loss is FEMA's modeled average dollars per year, not a count of past losses.
NRI's social vulnerability and resilience components come from other sources (CDC SVI and HVRI BRIC) and are not CHIP's SVI release.
CHIP publishes FEMA's values as released. It does not average, combine, or re-rank them, and does not derive state values.
Version v1.20 (December 2025). FEMA retired the NRI web application, and the data is distributed through OpenFEMA and FEMA's Resilience Analysis and Planning Tool (RAPT).
FEMA's v1.20 file repeats the national risk score in its risk state-percentile field for every county and tract, so CHIP does not show a within-state percentile for the overall risk score.

measures.label: National Risk Index score
measures.population: All U.S. counties or census tracts in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: National percentile rank (0–100) among areas at the same level.
measures.official_definition: FEMA National Risk Index composite score (RISK_SCORE, 0–100), combining expected annual loss, social vulnerability, and community resilience.
measures.interpretation: National percentile score (0–100) among areas at the same level; higher score means greater modeled natural-hazard risk. Not a forecast and not property-level risk.
measures.direction_note: Higher values indicate greater modeled natural-hazard risk.

measures.label: Expected annual loss score
measures.population: All U.S. states, counties, or census tracts in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: National percentile rank (0–100) among areas at the same level.
measures.official_definition: FEMA Expected Annual Loss composite score (EAL_SCORE, 0–100), representing the national percentile of modeled average annual natural-hazard loss.
measures.interpretation: National percentile score (0–100) among areas at the same level; higher values indicate greater modeled expected annual loss.
measures.direction_note: Higher values indicate greater modeled expected annual loss.

measures.label: Expected annual loss, percentile within state
measures.population: Counties or census tracts in the same state in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: Within-state percentile rank (0–100) among areas at the same level.
measures.official_definition: FEMA Expected Annual Loss composite state percentile (EAL_SPCTL, 0–100), comparing an area only with others in the same state.
measures.interpretation: Within-state percentile (0–100) among areas at the same level; higher values indicate greater modeled expected annual loss within the same state.
measures.direction_note: Higher values indicate greater modeled expected annual loss within the same state.

measures.label: Expected annual loss, total ($ per year)
measures.population: All U.S. states, counties, or census tracts in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: Modeled average annual economic loss across buildings, population equivalence, and agriculture (dollars per year).
measures.official_definition: FEMA Expected Annual Loss total composite value (EAL_VALT), in modeled average US dollars per year across all included natural hazards.
measures.interpretation: FEMA's modeled average dollars per year of natural-hazard loss, not a count of past losses. Higher values indicate greater modeled annual loss. Legend classes differ by geography level.
measures.direction_note: Higher values indicate greater modeled average annual loss in dollars.

measures.label: Social vulnerability score (as used by NRI)
measures.population: All U.S. counties or census tracts in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: National percentile rank (0–100) among areas at the same level.
measures.official_definition: Social vulnerability component score (SOVI_SCORE, 0–100) as incorporated by FEMA NRI from CDC/ATSDR SVI.
measures.interpretation: National percentile score (0–100) as used in FEMA NRI; higher values indicate greater social vulnerability. This is FEMA's NRI component, not CHIP's standalone CDC SVI release.
measures.direction_note: Higher values indicate greater social vulnerability (as used by NRI).

measures.label: Social vulnerability, percentile within state
measures.population: Counties or census tracts in the same state in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: Within-state percentile rank (0–100) among areas at the same level.
measures.official_definition: Social vulnerability state percentile (SOVI_SPCTL, 0–100) as published in FEMA NRI.
measures.interpretation: Within-state percentile (0–100) as used in FEMA NRI; higher values indicate greater social vulnerability within the same state.
measures.direction_note: Higher values indicate greater social vulnerability within the same state.

measures.label: Community resilience score
measures.population: All U.S. counties or census tracts in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: National percentile rank (0–100) among areas at the same level.
measures.official_definition: Community resilience component score (RESL_SCORE, 0–100) as incorporated by FEMA NRI from HVRI BRIC.
measures.interpretation: National percentile score (0–100) among areas at the same level; higher community resilience is better (greater capacity to prepare for, adapt to, and recover from natural hazards).
measures.direction_note: Higher values are better: a higher score indicates greater community resilience.

measures.label: Community resilience, percentile within state
measures.population: Counties or census tracts in the same state in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: Within-state percentile rank (0–100) among areas at the same level.
measures.official_definition: Community resilience state percentile (RESL_SPCTL, 0–100) as published in FEMA NRI.
measures.interpretation: Within-state percentile (0–100) among areas at the same level; higher community resilience is better compared with other areas in the same state.
measures.direction_note: Higher values are better: a higher percentile indicates greater community resilience within the same state.

measures.label: Community risk factor
measures.population: All U.S. counties or census tracts in FEMA NRI v1.20
measures.denominator: Scaling factor combining social vulnerability and community resilience (dimensionless multiplier).
measures.official_definition: FEMA Community Risk Factor (CRF_VALUE), a scaling factor derived from social vulnerability and community resilience that adjusts expected annual loss to produce the National Risk Index.
measures.interpretation: Dimensionless multiplier (typically ~0.5 to 2.0); higher values amplify expected annual loss into higher overall natural-hazard risk.
measures.direction_note: Higher values indicate a greater risk amplification factor.
